description: Write exact design-token values (colors, radius, fonts, icon library, layout density) onto a generated project. Use this when the user states concrete values ("make primary oklch(0.62 0.11 45)", "radius 12px"), or names a site whose theme to apply through `themePreset`. It merges over the current config and persists, so the change survives restarts and every later get-design-config returns it. Saved config is publicly readable by anyone with the fragment config URL. For vague direction ("warmer", "more playful"), iterate with the user toward concrete values first; do not invent numbers on their behalf.

config.description: Partial design config to merge over the current one. Only pass the fields the user changed. Colors are oklch() strings (e.g. 'oklch(0.62 0.11 45)'); radius is a CSS length (e.g. '0.75rem'); fonts are family names; density is compact, comfortable or spacious and overrides the design system's layout density.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

projectId.description: The project id returned by create-design-system.

themePreset.description: Optional. The name of a site whose measured theme to apply, such as 'Railway'. It sets the colors, and the radius and font when the theme has them. Values in `config` win over the theme. A name with no match changes nothing and returns close names.

name: set-design-config
title: Set a Project's Design Config
